analysis:
Compared both scanner revisions, diagnostics metadata/source/patch, and workflow metadata/patch. budget_scan.py now plans calls before source stages and each integration round (head 303–326, 332, 367), exports finished (112), and marks terminal execution even after caught failures (390–402). Citation validation, retained findings, coverage acknowledgment, uncertainty escalation, and integration convergence checks remain intact. diagnostics.py:80–88 adds completion and Bedrock policy/count fields without adding source, findings, raw response text, or credentials. The workflow removes paid manual dispatch and its PR-resolution code, preserves explicit fork opt-in for Bedrock, increases the job timeout, supplies a 3000-second scanner timeout, and switches from the configurable fixed call cap to workload planning with a 100-call ceiling (head 128–136).
No independently supported regression appears in these units. Provider authorization, attestation, hop-by-hop encryption, cache isolation, keys, billing ledger, inference cancellation, and fan-helper boundaries are not modified here; the indexed provider threats, including T-008, T-041 and T-052–T-058, do not directly describe this CI spending/control surface.
Integration must verify the native adapter's plan_calls contract: cumulative ceiling enforcement across models and integration rounds, cache-hit accounting, the single repair allowance, timeout enforcement, and safe numeric/fixed-string metrics exported to diagnostics. Those implementations are outside this batch, not observed missing controls. Also reconcile finished with report/gate consumers: budget_scan.py:400 means execution ended, not successful review; caught failures must remain incomplete through errors, coverage and pending-depth checks. Workflow checkout/authentication and clearance implementations were not supplied in full, so this local pass does not establish their behavior.
